Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
 Oral Judgment

Heard Smt.Suma.K learned counsel for the appellant who appears through video conference as well
as learned counsel Sri.H.C.Betsur who appears physically before this Court representing Sri.

Padma
S.Uttur learned counsel on record for respondent No.3.
2.

The mother of the deceased-Shivakumar who met with a road traffic accident and succumbed to
injuries
filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.12,70,000/- in total.

The Motor Accident
Claims Tribunal, Mysuru which dealt with the matter as Mvc No.634/2015 passed orders on
16.04.2019 holding that the claimant is entitled to Rs.11,51,000/- as compensation.
Aggrieved by the
same , the claimant is before this Court by way of appeal.

Making her submission with regard to the merits of the matter, learned counsel Smt.Suma.K
submits that the deceased as a coolie was earning Rs.500/- per day but without considering the said
fact, the Tribunal took the notional income as Rs.7,500/- per month and assessed compensation
which is erroneous.

Learned counsel also states that the accident occurred in the year 2015 and for
the relevant period, the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is taking the notional income as
Rs.9,000/- per month and considering the said figure, justice may be done to the appellant.

Learned
counsel Sri.H.C.Betsur for respondent No.3 did not raise any objection for taking the notional
income as Rs.9,000/- per month.

However, the learned counsel contended that besides awarding
Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of
love and affection which is unjustifiable.

Learned counsel seeks to take into account the said fact and
pass necessary orders.
4. It is not in dispute that the deceased-Shivakumar died at the age of 27 years.

Having considered
the fact that it is the right age to earn, this Court considers it desirable to take the notional income as

Thus applying the

Apply appropriate multiplier '17'
12,85,200-00
The loss of dependency thus comes to Rs.12,85,200/-.

Together with the said amount, the appellant is entitled to Rs.40,000/- towards loss
of filial consortium, Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.

Thus the total
amount which the appellant is entitled to is as under:

(i) The appeal is allowed in part.

Mysuru, through orders in Mvc No.634/2015, dated 16.04.2019 is enhanced from
